identity.note: P14-CLOSE RE-SCORE (2026-10-10). The 204/204 recorded at 9ee4952 predates the harness fix (xr-browser 3fe8d7e and b6cd40f, 2026-10-09: stale objects and unrestored builds counted false kills). Re-run with the fixed harness at xr-core a7ed1ab (which adds ledger_tag.cc and the S0 opacity fix), the identity core scored 220/248 = 88.71% with deny-guard 23/29, a FAIL. That transcript is evidence/P14/logs/t-mutation-identity-v3-rescore.json. A templates.cc survivor from it was re-checked by hand at 9ee4952 and survives there too, so the old 100% was an artifact. Tests were added (xr-core dec1d83, no behavior change) and the mint digest decoding became a tested function (S0 refactor, HG-S0-P14C-MINT-DECODE). The FULL matrix (sampled:false, seed 20261001) then scored 246/252 = 97.62% with deny-guard 29/29, a PASS. Six survivors remain, each an equivalent mutant (dispositions below).

survivors.disposition: equivalent-mutant: the std::sort comparator `a.kb > b.kb` becomes `>=`. The two differ only on equal kb, where std::sort leaves the order unspecified under either comparator, and the model's contract (biggest first; sum within total) says nothing about tie order. No deterministic test can tell them apart.

equivalent-mutant: BindingModel::CompactAudit `suggestions_.size() > keep_suggestions` becomes `>=`. At size == keep the mutant erases the empty range [begin, end - keep), the same outcome as skipping.
equivalent-mutant: CompactEvictions `size <= keep` becomes `<`. At size == keep the mutant computes dropped = 0, erases an empty range and returns 0, the same as the early return.

equivalent-mutant: DecodeDigestHex initializes `hi` to 1 instead of 0. HexNibble overwrites it on success, and on failure the function returns before reading it. The initializer is defensive only; no path reads it.
equivalent-mutant: the same as line 58, for `lo`.

equivalent-mutant: the tab sort comparator `<` becomes `<=`. Snapshot tab ids are unique (std::map keys), so equal ids never meet, and for hand-built docs with duplicate ids std::sort's order is unspecified under either comparator.
